prose.title: Cleon Ca$h Had the First Pick and Barely Needed Anything Else
prose.dek: Eric Mannila extended Bijan Robinson and Tucker Kraft, took Jeremiyah Love at 1.01, and spent {{f.team.0011.auction_spend}} at auction, less than any owner. The preseason simulation ranks Cleon Ca$h {{f.team.0011.power_rank|ord}}.

paragraphs: April was already strong. Mannila carried {{f.team.0011.active_roster_opening}} active players and {{f.team.0011.cap_opening}} in salary, with {{f.team.0011.studs_opening}} top-twelve starters: Justin Herbert, Bijan Robinson, an Elite RB1, CeeDee Lamb and Malik Nabers at receiver, Colston Loveland, an Elite TE1, and Tucker Kraft in a flex. Jaxson Dart was solid in the superflex. The {{f.team.0011.holes_opening}} holes were nobody at all at the second running back spot, and Wan'Dale Robinson in the other flex.

Before the draft he kept what he had. Robinson's rookie deal was extended at {{f.team.0011.contract_16161_salary}} this year and {{f.team.0011.contract_16161_tcv}} in all, and Kraft's at {{f.team.0011.contract_16222_salary}} for one more year. The other three expiring rookies, Kayshon Boutte, Marvin Mims and Will McDonald, went to the Expired Rookie Auction, two of them to Real Deal Creel. No trades, no cuts.

t.0011.slot_bridge.title: April: who held each priced slot

paragraphs: The draft filled the empty spot. Mannila held 1.01 and took Jeremiyah Love, the surest pick in the class: that slot has produced a usable player almost every time, and Love walked straight into the lineup as a High-end RB2. {{f.team.0011.rookie_picks_count}} picks in all, with Nicholas Singleton, Arvell Reese, already starting at linebacker, Zachariah Branch, Taylen Green, Jam Miller and Gabe Jacas after him.

The rest of the pre-auction offseason was quiet. No tags, no Expired Rookie Auction buys, one July trade, a 2027 fifth to Sex Manther for Efton Chism, and one release at no cost, Bralen Trice. He went into the auction with {{f.team.0011.active_roster_preauction}} active players and {{f.team.0011.cap_preauction}} committed.

t.0011.moves_s2.title: From the draft to the auction lock

paragraphs: Two restructures went with the auction, and they pointed in opposite directions. In June Herbert's deal was front-loaded to {{f.team.0011.contract_14779_salary}} this year and {{f.team.0011.contract_14779_tcv}} in all, and the day after the lock Robinson's was cut to {{f.team.0011.contract_16161_salary_2}} for 2026, which opened room. Opening room is not the same as using it, and here it was not used: Mannila spent {{f.team.0011.faa_spend}} at the Free Agent Auction, the least of any owner, and still has {{f.team.0011.cap_current_room}} of room.

Romeo Doubs took {{f.team.0011.faa_15779_price}} of it after twelve bids and signed long, {{f.team.0011.contract_15779_tcv}} in all. He is a replacement-level receiver and the one hole in the lineup. Kirk Cousins cost {{f.team.0011.faa_10700_price}}, Tyler Allgeier {{f.team.0011.faa_15712_price}}, and the kicker Cameron Dicker a little more than the minimum. The What it bought column is all depth, and the league table ranks the money {{f.team.0011.faa_off_rank|ord}} of {{f.league.teams}} for what each dollar added and {{f.team.0011.faa_off_gain_rank|ord}} for how much it added in all. For a lineup this complete, that was always going to be the result.

The lineup it built is the April lineup with the hole filled by the draft: {{f.team.0011.studs_today}} top-twelve starters in Herbert, Robinson, Lamb, Nabers, Loveland and Kraft, Love and Dart solid, and {{f.team.0011.holes_today}} hole, Doubs in the flex. His tight ends rank {{f.team.0011.te_rank|ord}} in the league and his backs {{f.team.0011.rb_rank|ord}}. The defense is thin, and since the simulation plays every starting spot, it counts.

t.0011.faa_value.title: What every owner's auction money bought

t.0011.moves_s3.title: From the auction to week one

captions.t.0011.faa_value: Ranked by how much each owner's starting offense improved between the auction lock and the close, for every dollar he spent on quarterbacks, backs, receivers and tight ends at the Free Agent Auction. What it bought sorts those buys by grade at their position: Elite, Very good, Good or Depth.

paragraphs: Mannila has been here since {{f.team.0011.hist_first_season}}, all {{f.team.0011.hist_seasons}} completed seasons, and the record is modest: {{f.team.0011.hist_playoffs}} playoff trip, no title, no division crown, and a {{f.team.0011.hist_allplay_pct}} career all-play record. On paper, this is the roster to change that.

DOG POUND 4 LIFE runs through C-Town, the simulation's {{f.league.power_rank_0009|ord}} team, and Cleon Ca$h is {{f.team.0011.power_rank|ord}}, with {{f.team.0011.sim_p_playoffs}} playoff odds and a {{f.team.0011.sim_p_division}} chance at the division. The Hawks are {{f.league.power_rank_0012|ord}}. He plays both five times.

The next three years, in Mannila's register, which is to say briefly. 2027: a playoff trip. He says it was probably luck. 2028: Love and Robinson are the best backfield in the league. He points out that C-Town was once, too. 2029: a title. One sentence about it, no follow-up.

Week one has not started for Cleon Ca$h. With {{f.league.wk_teams_final}} NFL teams done, none of his starters had played, and the two New England receivers who had, Chism and Doubs, were on his bench.

captions.t.0011.week1: Only games that had finished when this was written. A blank line means he recorded no scoring stat or did not play.
